summary.text: In September 2026, Barr expressed optimism that AI could enhance human potential, improve productivity, and raise living standards. In February and March 2026, he expected positive long-run economic effects while warning of significant labor-market disruption. In July 2026, he called for considering education, workforce, competition, and tax policies to spread AI's gains across workers, households, and communities. His April 2025 remarks advocated stronger defenses against AI-enabled financial fraud, including updated identity verification and increased penalties and enforcement.
